title: When Is Proof-Step Verification Worth Its Cost? Operating Requirements of Certify-or-Decline Verification for Open-Weight Mathematical Reasoning
abstract: arXiv:2611.14794v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Proof-step verification rewrites a solver's answer into typed steps and uses LLM judges to certify or decline. We evaluate this pipeline on open-weight models across GPQA, AIME-2025, and a MATH-500 subset. Certification raises answer-key-match precision by 31 percentage points on the strong GPQA configuration and 46 on AIME, while answering only 35% and 21% of attempts. On near-ceiling MATH-500, gains are at most 5 points at a loss of 13-27 points of coverage. An output-token-matched self-consistency selector obtains 82.9% precision at 35% coverage, compared with the verifier's pooled 87.6% (paired difference: +4.8 points, 95% interval [-8.2, 18.5]). A diagnostic sample reveals a distinct failure mode: 52 of 88 completed problems end in invalid proof construction without ever reaching a judge. Finally, external-LLM acceptance of rendered certified chains is 61.0-67.6%, compared with 87.6% answer-key match. These audits lack human or form

translated_title: 证明步骤验证何时才值得其成本？开源权重数学推理中“认证或拒绝”验证的运行条件
translated_abstract: 证明步骤验证将求解器的答案重写为带类型的步骤，并使用LLM裁判来认证或拒绝。我们在开源权重模型上跨GPQA、AIME-2025和MATH-500的一个子集评估了这一流程。认证使答案键匹配精确率在强GPQA配置上提升31个百分点，在AIME上提升46个百分点，但仅回答了35%和21%的尝试。在接近性能天花板的MATH-500上，增益最多为5个百分点，同时损失13-27个百分点的覆盖率。一个输出token数量匹配的自洽性选择器在35%覆盖率下取得82.9%的精确率，而验证器的汇总精确率为87.6%（配对差异：+4.8个百分点，95%区间为[-8.2, 18.5]）。一个诊断样本揭示了一种独特的失败模式：88个已完成问题中有52个以无效的证明构造告终，从未到达裁判环节。最后，外部LLM对渲染后的已认证证明链的接受率为61.0-67.6%，而对应的答案键匹配率为87.6%。这些审计缺乏人工或形式化验证……
tldr: “认证或拒绝”式证明步骤验证能大幅提升开源模型数学推理的精确率（GPQA提升31个百分点、AIME提升46个百分点），但代价是覆盖率骤降至35%和21%，且在近饱和的MATH-500上收益有限、相比简单的自洽性选择器并无显著优势，因此仅在高错误率场景下才值得使用。
en_tdlr: Certify-or-decline proof-step verification sharply improves precision (+31 pts on GPQA, +46 pts on AIME) at the cost of coverage (only 35% and 21% answered), yields limited gains on near-ceiling MATH-500, and shows no significant advantage over token-matched self-consistency, making it worthwhile only in high-error-rate regimes.
